turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: How may I help you?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um I'm here because I've had some numbness in my right hand and uh doesn't seem to be going going away, so I thought I should get it checked out by you.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yeah, certainly so, so when did this exactly start?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um so it's been pretty gradual, I would say over the past month or two months um is when I first noticed it, but the numbness is definitely worse now than it was at the start.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and uh where is this um the pain and numbness, where are you feeling it exactly?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um it's particular, it's the worst on my thumb and index finger.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, do you feel it on your ring finger or uh, or sorry or your middle finger?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um there is a little bit on my middle and ring finger, but it's like it's very very mild.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Uh, and uh, like how long, is, are the symptoms constant or or are they intermittent?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um I would say it's somewhat constant, but it's worse when um when I'm trying to like hold the steering wheel or using my phone, or you know, reading a book.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, I see, and um is there anything that you do uh at those times, to try to help get the symptoms to go away?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um I guess I like shake out my hand um or yeah, try to put pressure on those numb, numb areas.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, does flicking the the wrist or anything like that, does it help?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh maybe slightly.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And uh like how would you describe the the pains in your hand, like dull, achy, sharp?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I would say the pain is more like a tingling sensation. Um so I guess the tingling is is like a sharp feeling, um I wouldn't call it so much pain as I would just like tingling and numbness.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. OK, and uh is is there anything, so you mentioned sort of the driving and using your phone, are there any other activities that make it worse?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Recently I found it's hard for me to hold things um in my right hand, so like if I'm trying to open up a jar um like it's hard for me to hold it, and sometimes I find uh like it'll just fall out of my hand.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, so you're like dropping items and stuff?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Mhmm, yes.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and do you feel any, uh, like the numbness or tingling, does it radiate anywhere? Like to your forearm or up into your like upper arm or shoulder?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh no, I don't think so. No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And do you have any neck pain?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and have you had any trauma or injuries to your wrist or hand?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, nothing that I can think of.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright. Um and, have you had any weight loss recently?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: How about any fevers or chills?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Have you had any night sweats?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, have you had any changes to vision or hearing?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: How about other senses like any changes to your sense of smell or sense of taste?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright, have you had a runny nose or felt congested?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright, have you had a sore throat or a cough, perhaps?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright, have you had any shortness of breath?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Have you had any chest pain or feeling like you're uh like feeling like you have heart palpitations?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Have you had any lightheadedness or dizziness?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright, and have you had any nausea or vomiting?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: How about any abdominal pain?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright, how about any urinary problems?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Have you had any changes to your bowel movements like diarrhea, constipation?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and have you had any changes to your hair or nails?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And any skin rashes or um anything like that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright, and uh have you had any other pains in your joints or any joint swelling?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Uh, and have you been diagnosed with any medical conditions before?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, not that I can think of, yeah no, when I was younger I had like childhood asthma but nothing since.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, do you use any inhalers now?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, not for a long time.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, do you take any other medications?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, um and how about, do you have any allergies?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and have you had any surgeries or hospitalizations?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Um and, uh, could you tell me a little bit about uh where you're living and who you're living with?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: So um I live with my boyfriend and we live in a rented basement apartment downtown.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Um and are you working currently, or are you in school?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um I am a grad student.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, excellent, and um do you smoke cigarettes?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I don't.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and uh do you drink alcohol?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um I'll have a glass of wine once a week.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright. Um and do you use any recreational drugs?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And in the family, uh, are there any, is there a history of like hypothyroidism or other autoimmune conditions?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um there's rheumatoid arthritis in the family, but that's about it.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, um but you don't have any other joint swelling or pains, right?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Uh, and so next I would like to just um uh do a physical exam, and for the first part I'll ask you to just have a look at the hand and wrist and, are you seeing any swelling, erythema or redness or like any muscle wasting or or atrophy?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um so, in my right hand, um I guess the you know the fleshy part of your thumb just above your wrist, um that seems to be um I guess atrophied compared to my left hand.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK so, OK, so the muscle bulk is um reduced there.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Mhmm.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and are you feeling any temperature changes, like does the, any areas of the hand or wrist feel warm or hot?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright. Um and are there any areas if you uh palpate that cause pain, like over the wrist or any of the joints?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No pain. Um yeah, no pain.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright, um and, are you able to uh flex and extend your wrist?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh yeah I can do that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright, and and how about making a fist and and then also extending your fingers back out?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: That hurts, or like that causes the tingling.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, um are there any any issues with like moving your elbow or your shoulder?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and if you take your opposite hand, um with just your uh kind of pointer finger and middle finger and just really tap, um right near the wrist crease called the Tinel's test, you tap there. Do you feel any reproduction of symptoms?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, that that causes the tingling.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, so you're positive Tinel's test, and um if you kind of place your wrist so that um like the backs of your hands are facing each other so that your wrists are flexed downwards and your um, your wrists are flexed and your fingers are pointing towards the ground and you just hold that position for a period of time. Um do you feel any pain?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh I guess a little bit of tingling.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, so that would be a positive Phalen's test as well. Um and range of motion of the neck, do you have any problems with that or any pain there?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Um I think that was everything I wanted to ask about and check on the exam. Did you have any questions for me?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um no, no questions. Thank you so much.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright, you're welcome, yeah, so it sounds like this could be uh carpal tunnel syndrome and uh so we we may depending on uh kind of like nerve studies to confirm the diagnosis, and um things that you can do in the meantime would be to use like a splint or um yeah, try to use like nighttime splints and activity modification as well.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: OK, yeah, that sounds good.
